tools.name: plan_integration
tools.description: Returns the integration steps, code snippets and documentation links for adding Peppol to an application, for a single sender or for a platform that sends on behalf of its customers.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Searches the prose of the public getpeppr documentation and returns up to 5 matching pages, each with its url and a short excerpt. Excerpts carry no code: open the returned url, or call plan_integration, for code.

tools.name: validate_invoice
tools.description: Validates a Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL document against the Peppol rules, or a getpeppr invoice JSON against the SDK rules, and explains each violation. It does not check whether the invoice can be sent. Send sample or test invoices only, never a real invoice or real people's data.

tools.name: lookup_participant
tools.description: Says whether a Peppol identifier (scheme:identifier) is registered to receive documents on the production Peppol network, and which ones. A sandbox test customer is never on it, and send_test_invoice only targets the test receiver 9925:BE0314595348 whatever this answers.

tools.name: create_test_customer
tools.description: Platform accounts only: creates a test customer (sub-tenant legal entity) in the getpeppr sandbox and returns its registration state. Up to 10 active test customers per account; identifier rules per country: https://getpeppr.dev/docs/platform/legal-entities/. Calling it again with the same arguments

tools.name: send_test_invoice
tools.description: Sends an invoice in the getpeppr sandbox to the Belgian test receiver 9925:BE0314595348, for your own company or for one of your test customers. Never sends a real invoice. Lines without tax fields get your account's sandbox tax profile. While your sandbox tax profile is unchanged, calling it again

tools.name: get_document_status
tools.description: Returns the status and lifecycle events of a sandbox document sent from your getpeppr account; call it with the documentId send_test_invoice returned. submitted: getpeppr accepted it. delivered: the test receiver's access point received it, the goal of a sandbox test. failed: final, with a failureCa

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_docs · Private data: validate_invoice, lookup_participant, send_test_invoice, get_document_status · Public sink: validate_invoice, send_test_invoice.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_docs · Private data: validate_invoice, lookup_participant, send_test_invoice, get_document_status · Public sink: validate_invoice, send_test_invoice

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
